record_type_quote: Across two high-powered studies using the vignettes and key measures from Carlson and Zaki (2018), 3185 participants evaluated actors who engaged in neutral acts or helpful acts with or without self-interested motives for helping.

targets.title: Good deeds gone bad: Lay theories of altruism and selfishness
targets.evidence_quote: We replicate Carlson and Zaki's key findings: actors who help are perceived as more altruistic than those who engage in neutral acts, while those who help with self-interested motives are seen as less altruistic than those who do not help at all.
targets.outcome_quote: We replicate Carlson and Zaki's key findings: actors who help are perceived as more altruistic than those who engage in neutral acts, while those who help with self-interested motives are seen as less altruistic than those who do not help at all.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall replication verdict in abstract.
